patterns: is skimming the same as reading fast
entries.answer: To skim is to read quickly to get the shape of a text rather than its content, and it is a real skill aimed at a real decision: whether this is worth an hour. What you look for is structure, so the first and last paragraphs, the headings, and the first sentence of each section, since writers put their claims there. Skimming badly means reading every line quickly, which is slower than reading properly and remembers less.

entries.answer: Active reading means interacting with the text rather than moving across it, and the three moves that matter are questioning, annotating and summarising. The questioning is the one people skip, and it is where the gaps are found: asking why the author said that before reading on is what exposes an argument you would otherwise have skimmed past. Annotating is only worth doing if the mark means something, since a dog-eared page is a record that you were there and nothing more.

patterns: what is a good reading speed
entries.answer: Reading speed varies several-fold between people and, more usefully, between texts. A well-known argument at a familiar level is read slowly because it is being argued with, while a familiar narrative is read fast, so a single number says very little. The variable worth measuring is comprehension: speed gained at the cost of understanding is a loss, and this is why speed-reading courses that trade the first for the second tend to disappoint.

patterns: is close reading useful for exams
entries.answer: Close reading is reading a short passage repeatedly and closely, and it exists because meaning in literature often sits in what is unsaid. The method is to notice specific words, to ask what the sentence does rather than what it says, and to hold several readings at once. It is slow by design and is the opposite of skimming, so it is used on a few pages rather than on a chapter, and it is a poor way to cover a textbook.

patterns: how to write a good summary
how long should a summary be
is summarising the first sentence enough
entries.answer: A summary compresses a text to its main claim and its supporting structure, and a good one can be three sentences while a bad one is three sentences of introduction. The test is whether somebody who has not read it could reconstruct the argument, and if the summary only lists sections then it has captured the order rather than the reasoning. Most people summarise by writing the first sentence of each paragraph, which is a reasonable approximation and misses the parts where the writer actually convinced themselves of something.
